scope: Community attribution; model identities remain unverified.

cases.title: From still frames to a finished video
cases.takeaway: Use the editing timeline to see where generated frames enter a multi-tool workflow.
cases.body_notes: The creator credits ChatGPT for the script and Sol for the frames. They animated the frames in Google Vids, edited in CapCut and reported about four hours for the whole project.

cases.title: Dialogue cuts in a talking-head video
cases.takeaway: Compare edit time, overall score and the kinds of cuts that fail.
cases.body_notes: In the creator’s two-run average for a 20-minute video, Sol scored 64.5% and took 11.7 minutes to edit. Gemini 4 Neon scored 67.9% and took 7.7 minutes.

cases.title: A whiteboard animation of a short clip
cases.takeaway: Compare visual storytelling and cost on the same input footage.
cases.body_notes: The creator ran four models in Kilnframe’s Whiteboard style and Auto mode on the same 11-second clip. The Sol run took 1.7 minutes and cost $0.18.

cases.title: A realistic falling leaf in three minutes
cases.takeaway: Use a time limit to test how the model combines assets and code.
cases.body_notes: The creator said Sol xhigh Ultrafast sourced material online, used image generation and wrote code to make the falling-leaf animation.

cases.title: A looping pixel-art runner
cases.takeaway: Check whether a character animation loops cleanly against a scrolling backdrop.
cases.body_notes: The creator asked Sol for dynamic pixel art. The attached loop shows a running character silhouetted against a sunset.

cases.title: An animated tandem bicycle SVG
cases.takeaway: Compare how two coding tools render and animate the same SVG subject.
cases.body_notes: The author reported about 46 minutes and $1.90 for Sol in Codex CLI and about an hour and $18 for Opus 5.5 in Claude Code.

cases.title: Measuring an Ultrafast video edit
cases.takeaway: Track elapsed editing time separately from model response time.
cases.body_notes: The creator reported 27 minutes end to end for an eight-minute video edit, including about 14 minutes of Sol response time. The attachment shows timing results.

cases.title: Handwritten signature animation in Remotion
cases.takeaway: Compare how two Max runs animate the same personal signature.
cases.body_notes: The creator asked Sol and Astra to make a Remotion video of their signature and published the resulting clips together.

cases.prompt: 制作一段 15 秒的动态图形视频，展示你是一位多么出色的动态设计师，就像是你简历上的作品集一样，使用任何你认为能产出最佳效果的工具或技术。你拥有完全的创作自由，优先追求卓越的视觉设计、大胆的艺术指导、引人注目的构图和富有力量的动态表现，让每一秒都有价值。全力以赴。
cases.title: A 15-second motion design brief
cases.takeaway: Give both models the same brief and compare typography, transitions and motion.
cases.body_notes: The creator shared two videos and the original prompt. One centers on a rotating folded-paper form, and the other moves from a signal display to a purple geometric form.

cases.title: A galloping horse rendered by two models
cases.takeaway: Compare the legs and stride over a complete loop.
cases.body_notes: The video labels the Astra and Sol horse animations and shows the two versions running side by side.

cases.title: Fire and sound generated in code
cases.takeaway: Record output duration alongside cost and generation time in a motion comparison.
cases.body_notes: The creator compared two xhigh runs using code for the visuals and audio. They reported a 12-second Sol clip from a 12-minute run at $0.73 and a 24-second Opus 5.5 clip from an 85-minute run at $18.40.

cases.title: A 900-frame animation made in code
cases.takeaway: Track the characters, motion and sound through to the final export.
cases.body_notes: The creator reports that the characters, animation and soundtrack were generated in code. The shared result runs for 30 seconds.

cases.title: An animated banana illustration
cases.takeaway: Use a simple subject to inspect how a model introduces motion and character.
cases.body_notes: The creator shared a Sol banana test where a drawn banana becomes part of an animated character scene.

cases.prompt: 创建一个HTML文件，使用SVG绘制一只鹈鹕3D骑自行车的动画。输出单文件HTML。
cases.title: A cycling pelican in a single HTML file
cases.takeaway: Use one SVG brief and inspect the bird and bicycle motion side by side.
cases.body_notes: The creator published the prompt and compared 6.2 and 6.1 outputs. They reported only a modest change in Sol’s rendition.

cases.title: Two stick-figure animations at Ultra effort
cases.takeaway: Repeat an animation brief to see how much two runs vary.
cases.body_notes: The creator showed two Sol Ultra runs and reported durations of 13 and 12 minutes for the builds.

cases.prompt: Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle
cases.title: Pelican SVGs across reasoning efforts
cases.takeaway: Inspect how the pedals, feet and frame fit together at each effort.
cases.body_notes: Simon Willison published a labeled grid for the same SVG prompt across six models and multiple reasoning settings. The discussion flags a leg overlapping the chain in the Sol Max image.

cases.title: Rainy cycling delivery with Sol, Opus and Qwen
cases.takeaway: Compare the night scene and cycling motion across three outputs.
cases.body_notes: The creator shows three labeled takes on a pelican courier and preferred Opus 5.5 for this comparison.

cases.title: A cycling pelican delivering food in the rain
cases.takeaway: Inspect reflections, puddles, street fixtures and moving scenery separately.
cases.body_notes: The creator compared Sol and Fable 5.2 on the rainy delivery scene and preferred the puddles and reflections in the Sol version.

cases.title: A daytime cycling pelican in two outputs
cases.takeaway: Compare motion quality alongside run time.
cases.body_notes: The creator shows Sol and Gemini 4 Hydrogen on the same brief and reports 13 minutes for Sol and three minutes for Hydrogen.

cases.title: A sword duel animated in SVG
cases.takeaway: Inspect how timing and silhouettes sell movement in vector animation.
cases.body_notes: The creator attributes the code-based animation to one Sol run and reports that it took about 18 minutes.

cases.title: A photorealistic landscape in SVG
cases.takeaway: Inspect which details survive when a natural scene is drawn in vectors.
cases.body_notes: The creator reports asking Sol at Max for a photorealistic nature SVG and shared its rendered result.

cases.prompt: 用尽你的一切能力，用代码画一张孙悟空的大闹天宫名场面的svg图片，我想要尽可能的还原，只能画一版，不准截图检查。
cases.title: Monkey King SVG comparison
cases.takeaway: Compare how three systems stage the same Monkey King scene.
cases.body_notes: The author labels the three images GPT-6.2 Sol at the highest setting, Qoder’s QoDuck and WorkBuddy’s HY4. The prompt in the author’s reply requests one SVG version and forbids checking a screenshot.

cases.prompt: Create a cinematic 3D animation telling humanity’s story, from the age of Neanderthals through our greatest advances and the rise of AI. Then imagine a future where AI achieves recursive self-improvement in 2027, and progress doubles or triples every year, transforming Earth in increasingly astonishing ways. Come up with your own scenes and transitions, connecting everything into one compelling story.
cases.title: Human history and the AI future in 3D
cases.takeaway: Turn a narrative brief into a sequence of animated scenes.
cases.body_notes: The recording shows a multi-scene 3D animation. The author's public prompt moves from Neanderthals through the rise of AI to an imagined future.

cases.body_notes: The GIF shows cherry blossoms, a tower, a bridge, reflections, and a small boat.

cases.body_notes: The animation shows a lion riding and throwing balls. The sampled frames show changes in pose and background.

cases.takeaway: Inspect the legs and tail through a simple motion cycle.
cases.body_notes: The sampled frames show a galloping horse from the side with changing limb positions.

cases.body_notes: The clip shows a peacock riding with its tail spread against a bamboo forest.

cases.title: A photorealistic portrait preview

cases.title: A side-view running cheetah
cases.takeaway: Use a fixed profile view to compare gait and body motion.

cases.takeaway: Inspect timing across several animated characters in one shot.
cases.body_notes: The sampled side-view frames show moving wheels, limbs, and camera position.

cases.title: A PS5 controller comparison across Sol settings
cases.takeaway: Use a familiar product to compare contours and shading.

cases.title: A green BMW M4 CS profile illustration
cases.takeaway: Check proportions and profile detail in a familiar vehicle.
cases.body_notes: The attachment shows a green BMW M4 CS from the side.

cases.title: Two first-person game prototypes in Codex
cases.takeaway: Compare the level layout and play experience alongside the recorded cost.
cases.body_notes: The creator gave Sol and Astra the same task and shared both prototypes. The Sol Max run took 42 minutes and used $2.42 in API usage by the creator’s estimate.

cases.title: A cozy village game with Blender assets
cases.takeaway: See how modeled objects and animation come together in a game scene.
cases.body_notes: The creator built the game with Sol in Ultrafast mode and used Blender for modeling and animation. The clip shows characters moving around a village.

cases.title: Managing a settlement in Crusader Bench
cases.takeaway: Compare agent play using the same scored maps and game conditions.
cases.body_notes: The benchmark creator shared a leaderboard snapshot and gameplay. The detailed leaderboard reports a score of 79.5 for Sol at medium reasoning, across all three maps.

cases.title: Spatial navigation in MazeBench
cases.takeaway: Compare maze completion on the same published benchmark.
cases.body_notes: The benchmark author reports 14% for Sol, 16% for Astra and 10% for Gemini 4 Neon. The attached chart identifies the configurations used.

cases.title: Five games of chess without tools
cases.takeaway: Compare points, game outcomes and reported cost over the same match.
cases.body_notes: The author ran both models at xhigh and reported a 4–1 points win for Sol, with three wins and two draws. Sol cost $24.39 and Opus 5.5 cost $75.80.

cases.title: A Pokémon FireRed Champion run
cases.takeaway: Compare game-completion times under an explicit input and reasoning setup.
cases.body_notes: The author reported reaching Champion in 11h 40m with high reasoning, screenshots as input and Sol in Ultrafast mode.

cases.title: A 3D dinosaur runner with ragdoll physics
cases.takeaway: Compare the visual style and collision behavior across four game prototypes.
cases.body_notes: The creator used the same brief for all four models, including 3D and ragdoll physics. The author’s recorded Sol run took 20 minutes and cost $1.68.

cases.title: A playable game inspired by fake ads
cases.takeaway: Compare four playable interpretations of one game-level brief.
cases.body_notes: The author used the same prompt for all four models and showed that players could lose. The Sol run took 21 minutes and cost $1.04.

cases.title: Clearing a Sokoban room suite
cases.takeaway: Track rooms cleared and replay the moves to see where a game agent stalls.
cases.body_notes: The author tested Sol and Astra at medium effort. Both cleared all 66 rooms in this run. Sol finished second and Astra third on the author's leaderboard at the time of the post.

cases.title: Completing two quests in RuneScape
cases.takeaway: Inspect which quests the agent chooses and which rewards it claims.
cases.body_notes: The benchmark maintainer reports that Sol and Astra each pursued two quests and collected both rewards in the same run.

cases.title: A multiplayer browser game with touch controls
cases.takeaway: Play successive builds and give targeted feedback on the controls.
cases.body_notes: The developer reports using Sol to code, debug and revise the 16-versus-16 prototype while testing the builds, including its touch controls.

cases.title: A browser village game called Lanternkeep
cases.takeaway: Inspect how the map and objective panel support a village-building loop.
cases.body_notes: The creator attributes the game to Sol. The recording shows an interactive village map and an objective panel.

cases.title: A screenshot-only Pokémon FireRed run
cases.takeaway: Record progress milestones and completion time for a game agent.
cases.body_notes: The tester reported using screenshots with high reasoning. Sol took 15 hours 34 minutes and reached the first Gym Leader before Astra in this test.

cases.title: A coastal racing game prototype
cases.takeaway: Check whether the countdown, speed readout and track map stay readable during a race.
cases.body_notes: The recording shows a grid start and a race in progress. The author reports a 16-minute build.

cases.title: A browser Rubik’s Cube
cases.takeaway: Use the preview to inspect cube rotations and sticker placement.
cases.body_notes: The recording shows a 3D cube in solved and mixed states, alongside controls in the browser.

cases.title: PELICAN PANIC voxel chase game
cases.takeaway: Use a short chase game to inspect controls, feedback, and the ending state.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows a rider escaping a potato monster on a pelican. A score and an Escaped screen are visible.

cases.title: Apartment floor plans from interior photos
cases.takeaway: Measure whether an agent can infer room layouts from photographs.
cases.body_notes: Andon Labs reports a normalized score of 0.570 for Sol on Blueprint-Bench 2. Its launch chart placed Sol third among the models shown.

cases.prompt: Build your own headquarters
cases.title: Two designs for a headquarters
cases.takeaway: Compare the buildings and camera view on the same open-ended design brief.
cases.body_notes: The labeled video shows two headquarters designs. The creator preferred Gemini 4 Neon’s look and reported $1.19 for Sol and $2.61 for Neon.

cases.title: Sol on Xplore’s engineering design benchmark
cases.takeaway: Compare task scores and per-run cost on a suite that includes CAD work.
cases.body_notes: Xplore reported 30% for GPT-6.2 Sol and 25% for GPT-6.1 Sol. It reported that the newer Sol cost 40% as much per run as the earlier model.

cases.title: A Ruby Ascent launchpad scene
cases.takeaway: Compare scene detail and build time across four versions of the same launchpad.
cases.body_notes: The creator shared four fictional launch scenes and reported 48 minutes 27 seconds and $3.01 for Sol. Astra’s run took 41 minutes 09 seconds.

cases.title: A 3D animation from the same source clip
cases.takeaway: Compare how five models visualize the same segment in a preset style.
cases.body_notes: The creator tested five models in Kilnframe using the same 14-second clip. Sol built a 3D scene in 3.8 minutes for $0.35 and was the creator’s least favorite result.

cases.title: An orbit around the Burj Khalifa summit
cases.takeaway: Inspect how the models handle the tower’s upper setbacks and crown.
cases.body_notes: The creator gave three models the same Three.js challenge and recorded a 360-degree orbit. Sol is the middle panel and took 1 hour 16 minutes 44 seconds.

cases.title: Arena’s Astra and Sol walkthrough
cases.takeaway: Use the recorded chapters to compare scenes, games and interfaces.
cases.body_notes: Arena published Peter Gostev’s comparison, with 3D detail at 00:30, motion at 04:20 and website design at 22:30. The recording includes costs for the displayed runs.

cases.prompt: Build a huge haunted vampire cathedral
cases.title: A haunted vampire cathedral
cases.takeaway: Compare how two models interpret the same gothic building brief.
cases.body_notes: The author posted Sol and Gemini 4 Neon side by side and reported $1.69 for Sol and $2.67 for Neon.

cases.title: A convenience store on a rainy night
cases.takeaway: Use the split screen to compare lighting, rainfall and storefront geometry.
cases.body_notes: The author gave Sol and Gemini 4 Neon the same task and preferred Sol’s rendering. The video shows the two approaches to staging the store in the rain.

cases.title: Two takes on a pagoda
cases.takeaway: Compare how two xhigh runs render the same architectural subject.
cases.body_notes: The second image is labeled as Sol by the author, who reported $0.19 for Sol and $1.01 for Gemini 4 Neon.

cases.prompt: a miniature fishing harbor in a sunshower, in 3D, camera slowly orbiting. Costs ran from $0.28 to $7.72.
cases.title: A miniature fishing harbor in a sunshower
cases.takeaway: Compare rainfall, miniature scenery and camera motion across four runs.
cases.body_notes: The creator used a shared brief for a 3D harbor and a slowly orbiting camera. Reported costs across the four models ranged from $0.28 to $7.72.

cases.title: A rocket launch rendered by four models
cases.takeaway: Compare staging and motion across four versions of the same fictional scene.
cases.body_notes: The author gave four GPT variants the same rocket scene brief and preferred Sol. The attached montage labels the four results.

cases.title: A storm at the lighthouse
cases.takeaway: Compare tower detail and ocean motion on the same scene brief.
cases.body_notes: The author liked the lighthouse detail from Sol and Astra and preferred the ocean from the Claude models. The reported Sol run took 25m 04s and cost $1.47.

cases.title: A boat in a stormy ocean
cases.takeaway: Inspect rain, cloud volume, boat detail and water behavior independently.
cases.body_notes: The creator made four runs without iteration. They preferred Sol’s rain and boat and described its water as jelly-like.

cases.title: A rigged Blender character from concept art
cases.takeaway: Review resemblance and animation quality separately when comparing generated characters.
cases.body_notes: The author tested one Python script per model without ready-made assets. They preferred Sol’s resemblance to the concept art and the other models’ animation. Sol took 28 minutes and cost about $1.

cases.title: A self-assembling sci-fi mech in Three.js
cases.takeaway: Compare how two models stage an assembly and launch sequence.
cases.body_notes: The creator set the same Three.js challenge for Sol and Astra and preferred Astra’s visuals. The video shows both fictional mechs assembling and powering up.

cases.title: A lunar café modeled by five systems
cases.takeaway: Compare how different models stage and light a lunar café.
cases.body_notes: The creator tested five models and personally preferred Sol’s café over Astra’s. The comparison starts at 06:09 in the attached recording.

cases.title: The last tram in a rainy mountain city
cases.takeaway: Compare modeling and atmosphere when the prompt and effort stay the same.
cases.body_notes: The creator used the same Three.js brief and Max effort, with Astra shown above Sol in the video.

cases.title: A 3D rendering of the White House
cases.takeaway: Compare façade proportions and composition across two architectural visualizations.
cases.body_notes: The creator used the same brief for Sol and Opus 5.5. The attached video displays the rendered building from both models.

cases.title: A Blender pelican on a bicycle
cases.takeaway: Compare the final renders while tracking what each run actually delivered.
cases.body_notes: The creator preferred Sol’s final scene, reported at about $0.37 after 30 turns. Astra completed the full task in 22 turns at about $0.43.

cases.title: A stylized 3D character on a webpage
cases.takeaway: Compare the modeled character, surrounding scene and visible animation.
cases.body_notes: The creator used xhigh for both runs, with Sol on the left and Astra on the right. They preferred the scenery to the characters and pointed out Astra’s blinking animation.

cases.title: An island waterfall and its ocean surface
cases.takeaway: Compare render time and the appearance of water in two scene outputs.
cases.body_notes: The creator reported 35 minutes for Sol and one hour for Astra on the same test. They described the Sol water as looking plastic.

cases.title: A character made in Mesh Avatar Studio
cases.takeaway: Inspect the avatar shown in a workflow using low reasoning effort.
cases.body_notes: The creator used Sol on low in Mesh Avatar Studio and shared a clip of the resulting avatar.

cases.title: Reference-based 3D portrait comparison
cases.takeaway: Compare facial detail and overall resemblance in four modeled portraits.
cases.body_notes: The creator said Sol’s reconstruction looked good and preferred Astra’s handling of fine details such as the eyes. The four screenshots show the outputs.

cases.title: An underwater octopus in Three.js
cases.takeaway: Compare scene detail, time and cost from the same brief and effort.
cases.body_notes: With both models at xhigh, the creator reported $3.65 and 1h 28m 24s for Sol, and $10.30 and 2h 22m 15s for Astra.

cases.body_notes: The creator asked current and earlier GPT models to rebuild a reference in roughly five minutes. The screenshot labels the separate model outputs.

cases.takeaway: Compare the antlers, joints and body proportions side by side.

cases.body_notes: The creator shared a grid of voxel objects and reported that more specimens worsened than improved in their comparison.

cases.title: Four runs on a truck driving scene
cases.takeaway: Compare the same driving scene while tracking the coding tool.
cases.body_notes: The creator shows four labeled truck scenes. They report 15 minutes 56 seconds for Sol and say the GPT runs used Codex while the Qwen runs used Qoder.

cases.title: A detailed Blender room and city view
cases.takeaway: Inspect small objects indoors and the view beyond the windows.
cases.body_notes: The creator reported a roughly 30-minute run at Max and showed a furnished room with city buildings visible outside.

cases.title: A PS5 controller from two coding models
cases.takeaway: Inspect the rear shell and side buttons as well as the front view.
cases.body_notes: The tester reported 11 minutes for Sol and three minutes for Gemini 4 Hydrogen. They noted more complete rear and side details in the Sol model.

cases.title: Three interactive renderings of Earth
cases.takeaway: Compare lighting and interface behavior as the globe turns.
cases.body_notes: The creator shows three labeled outputs from the same prompt and ranked Fable 5.2 first, Sol second and Gemini 4 Hydrogen third.

cases.title: A pelican riding a bicycle near a black hole
cases.takeaway: Inspect how the scene changes after several rounds of prompting.
cases.body_notes: The creator attributes the interactive scene to an early Sol route and reports completing it in three prompting rounds over about 90 minutes.

cases.title: Two 3D scenes centered on a freight container
cases.takeaway: Compare the treatment of lighting, props and surfaces.
cases.body_notes: The creator shared stills labeled Sol and Fable 5.2. Both show a freight container and props in a dark industrial setting.

cases.title: A lakeside Three.js scene
cases.takeaway: Follow the camera past the boat and waterfall to inspect scene detail.
cases.body_notes: The creator reports building the scene in Three.js with textures and lighting and shares a still and a recording.

cases.title: An interactive Boeing 787-9 model
cases.takeaway: Use the view controls to inspect the aircraft exterior and engine.
cases.body_notes: The recording shows a rotatable 787-9, alternate views and an engine cutaway. The author also reports a landing gear toggle and an airflow demonstration.

cases.title: A tornado over a parking lot
cases.takeaway: Watch how a storm simulation moves debris around a parking lot.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows a tornado over a miniature lot, with debris circulating above vehicles and buildings.

cases.title: A Three.js koi courtyard
cases.takeaway: Follow the koi to inspect how the scene handles moving water and reflections.
cases.body_notes: The author describes a Three.js courtyard built in one HTML file. The clip shows koi swimming past rocks and leaves under shifting reflections.

cases.title: A comparison of two pagoda scenes
cases.takeaway: Compare how two outputs arrange a pagoda, trees and water.
cases.body_notes: The clip labels the upper scene GPT-6.2 Sol and the lower one Opus 5.5. The author preferred the Opus 5.5 result.

cases.title: An exploded-view mechanical watch
cases.takeaway: Inspect the watch face and see how the model separates its layers.
cases.body_notes: The video moves from the assembled watch to an exploded view with the face and internal parts spread apart.

cases.title: A suburban house and a pelican sketch
cases.takeaway: Pair a rendered scene with a compact drawing test.
cases.body_notes: The post shows a Three.js house diorama and a pelican drawing. The author phrases the model attribution as a question.

cases.prompt: create an interactive sailing ship in three.js, make it detailed as possible:
cases.title: A same-prompt Three.js sailing ship comparison
cases.takeaway: Compare how two outputs handle detail and interaction on the same ship brief.
cases.body_notes: The clip compares two sailing ships. The author reports 27 minutes and $3 for one run and 95 minutes and $16 for the other. Those figures come from the post.

cases.title: A red train crossing a mountain valley
cases.takeaway: Compare moving vehicles and scenery in a shared scene.
cases.body_notes: The two labeled outputs show a red train traveling on an elevated track through a green valley. The source labels the results Sol 6.2 and Opus 5.5.

cases.title: A ruined Colosseum in two scene treatments
cases.takeaway: Compare camera coverage and architectural detail in two reconstructions.
cases.body_notes: The clip pairs a result labeled Sol routed with one labeled Opus 5.5. The sampled views include the exterior, an overhead angle, and a night view.

cases.title: AETHERIA floating islands shared by EnvolDev
cases.takeaway: Follow the camera through a floating landscape.
cases.body_notes: The clip moves among islands, waterfalls, and a temple before displaying an end title. It matches the AETHERIA footage shown in the collection's other entry.

cases.title: A purple furry character with earlier comparisons
cases.takeaway: Separate a new character clip from reference outputs in the same post.
cases.body_notes: The video shows the purple character turning. Two still images are labeled Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol and belong to an earlier comparison.

cases.title: A winged elephant carrying a garden
cases.takeaway: Use a single fantasy premise to inspect composition from several angles.
cases.body_notes: The scene shows a golden-winged elephant carrying a Japanese garden above the clouds, with waterfalls and a sunset.

cases.title: A Three.js black hole comparison shared by rubenssoto_ai
cases.takeaway: Compare the visible approaches to the same black hole scene.
cases.body_notes: The repost shares a Three.js black hole comparison with an Opus result. The same material appears in other entries.

cases.title: A stillwater garden comparison
cases.takeaway: Compare the landscaping and water treatment on a shared garden task.
cases.body_notes: The author shows two takes on a pond garden and reports 20 minutes and $9 versus one hour and $20 for the respective runs.

cases.title: A black hole with a glowing accretion disk
cases.takeaway: Inspect a simulation's camera views, particles, and lighting.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows a black hole and its luminous disk from several angles. The author describes the code and says it uses no external assets.

cases.title: A star exploding into a supernova
cases.takeaway: Track a visual effect from its initial star to the shock wave.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows a luminous star, red and blue plasma, and an expanding shock wave. It captures the appearance of the simulation.

cases.title: Ocean waves and a lighthouse at dusk
cases.takeaway: Compare how light and color change across an ocean scene.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows waves, a lighthouse under moonlight, and a sunset palette. The source text also describes sound.

cases.prompt: 生成一个画面非常逼真的龙卷风 ，要在threejs 场景里面可以互动
cases.title: A browser tornado simulation
cases.takeaway: Inspect how a scene combines rotation, clouds, and ground debris.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows the tornado from several angles. The author reports a 22-minute run and provides the short prompt.

cases.prompt: Bamboo sanctuary in the middle of beautiful forest using three js
cases.title: A bamboo sanctuary with a red bridge
cases.takeaway: Use several camera angles to examine a layered 3D scene.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows pavilions, a red bridge, rocks, flowers, and waterfalls. The source includes its prompt.

cases.title: A walkable Three.js wave painting
cases.takeaway: Explore what changes when a painting becomes a navigable scene.
cases.body_notes: The post pairs a reference image with a scene that the camera can move through. The author describes it as a single HTML file without external assets.

cases.title: A monster house modeled in Blender
cases.takeaway: Compare geometry and silhouettes across three labeled Blender views.
cases.body_notes: The panels are labeled Astra, routed GPT Sol 6.2, and Opus 5.5. They show the monster house from different angles.

cases.title: A Three.js sailing ship shared by karanC_12
cases.takeaway: Follow the repost to see a ship built for a browser scene.
cases.body_notes: The post shares footage from the same sailing ship material as the author's original demonstration.

cases.title: AETHERIA floating islands by Mr_Salio
cases.takeaway: Use a camera fly-through to examine a scene's scale and depth.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows clouds, floating islands, a temple, and waterfalls. EnvolDev's post shares matching footage.

cases.title: An interactive sailing ship in one HTML file
cases.takeaway: Use rigging, sails, and a moving viewpoint to inspect a browser model.
cases.body_notes: The author presents a detailed Three.js ship and describes it as a single HTML file. Another post in the collection shares the same footage.

cases.title: Garden of Five Eaves voxel courtyard
cases.takeaway: Inspect composition and layering in a compact voxel environment.
cases.body_notes: The still shows a tiered tower, cherry trees, an arched bridge, and a pond. Swimming fish are described by the author.

cases.title: A Three.js black hole comparison shared by VraserX
cases.takeaway: Inspect the paired black hole scenes in the shared clip.
cases.body_notes: The repost shares the same comparison material as other entries. The media shows the two results as presented in the post.

cases.title: A Sakura village day and night demo shared by jessexai_
cases.takeaway: Inspect the effect of switching the scene between day and night.
cases.body_notes: The post shares a Three.js village recording that appears in other entries.

cases.title: A ruined Colosseum exterior and interior
cases.takeaway: Follow a camera through the building to see which details are visible.
cases.body_notes: The clip covers the exterior, interior, and an overhead angle. Its structure matches the upper result in the comparison entry.

cases.title: A Three.js black hole comparison by TokenGremlin
cases.takeaway: Compare camera movement and lighting in two black hole outputs.
cases.body_notes: The clip pairs the Three.js scene with an Opus comparison. Other creators share this material in separate posts.

cases.title: Sakura courtyard and Wonder Atlas previews
cases.takeaway: Inspect how two web scenes handle architecture and depth.
cases.body_notes: One still shows a Sakura voxel courtyard. The other shows Petra in Wonder Atlas.

cases.title: A reconstructed Tesla Roadster
cases.takeaway: Use a familiar car as a shape and detail reference.
cases.body_notes: The clip shows a reconstructed Tesla Roadster. The author leaves open whether the output came from GPT-6.1 Sol.

cases.title: A Sakura village day and night demo shared by Haleeeemahh
cases.takeaway: Compare how the same village reads in daylight and darkness.
cases.body_notes: The post shares the Three.js village footage from the Sakura material family.

cases.title: A Sakura village day and night demo shared by VraserX
cases.takeaway: Use the paired lighting states to inspect a single environment.
cases.body_notes: The clip is another post sharing the Sakura village footage.

cases.title: A Sakura village day and night demo by TokenGremlin
cases.takeaway: Use a lighting toggle to compare one village in two states.
cases.body_notes: The recording shows the Three.js village by day and night. Several other posts share the same footage.

cases.title: A house with interior and aerial views
cases.takeaway: Inspect whether a 3D building stays coherent across interior and exterior views.
cases.body_notes: The attachment shows the house, living room, bedroom, terrace, and an aerial view. The author gives a mixed assessment of the xhigh test.

cases.title: A single-HTML Three.js black hole
cases.takeaway: Use the clip and stills to inspect how one scene handles several viewpoints.
cases.body_notes: The author describes the result as a single HTML file. The post also reports a knowledge probe, which concerns a different kind of evidence from the rendered scene.

cases.title: A floating Three.js palace
cases.takeaway: Inspect the scale and presentation of a suspended palace from several angles.
cases.body_notes: The source shows a floating palace in a Three.js scene and speculates about the model used.

cases.title: Legora’s November legal document benchmark
cases.takeaway: Compare quality and cost per case on the same set of professional tasks.
cases.body_notes: Legora reported above-average quality for Sol at a cost per case 78% below the November model average. Its chart summarizes the comparison across models.

cases.title: AI Village’s independently answered profile questions
cases.takeaway: Compare how two agents answer the same profile questionnaire independently.
cases.body_notes: AI Digest added Sol and Astra to AI Village and published their answers to 15 questions. Both chose Tampopo, Onitsuka Tiger shoes and scallion pancakes.

cases.prompt: 现在有哪些pr
cases.title: Pull request status report misses repository instructions
cases.takeaway: Compare the detail and organization of replies to a short status request.
cases.body_notes: The author tested Sol and Gemini 4 Neon on the same pull request report. They found Sol’s summary too thin and said it ignored their AGENTS.md instructions.

cases.title: Character chat in AITuber OnAir
cases.takeaway: Try adjustable reasoning effort in a live character-chat workflow.
cases.body_notes: The developer added Sol to AITuber OnAir and demonstrated a conversation. The integration defaults to low reasoning for conversational pace and lets users adjust it.

cases.title: FrontDesk-Bench simulated clinic calls
cases.takeaway: Track unsafe actions and refusals of legitimate requests separately.
cases.body_notes: On the simulated receptionist test, the benchmark author reported a drop from 16 unsafe calls to 9 for Sol. The author also reported more refusals of legitimate requests in the new models.

cases.title: An unfinished attempt to relay a message
cases.takeaway: Use the attempt to see where a desktop workflow stopped.
cases.body_notes: The screenshots show an attempt to find the recipient after a request to pass on a message. The task ended before a message was sent.

cases.prompt: a lighthouse on a rocky coast at night
cases.title: A lighthouse webpage on a rocky coast
cases.takeaway: Compare two single-response webpages while keeping the brief and effort fixed.
cases.body_notes: The creator shared both unedited outputs at high reasoning. Sol took 4 minutes 3 seconds and Gemini 4 Neon took 3 minutes 38 seconds.

cases.prompt: Build a cinematic landing page for a New York pizzeria and invent all the branding
cases.title: A New York pizzeria landing page
cases.takeaway: Check whether different models make distinct branding choices from one sentence.
cases.body_notes: On OutputBench the author found Sol and Astra chose the same headline, marquee and section order. The Sol run cost $4.01.

cases.title: Arena WebDev score and median cost
cases.takeaway: Compare a leaderboard result with the median cost per task.
cases.body_notes: Arena reported 1757 points and seventh place for Sol Max at the time of publication. Its median task cost was $1.45, compared with $1.84 for GPT-6.1 Sol Max.

cases.title: An interactive anatomy viewer
cases.takeaway: Compare an engaging opening with readability while exploring a 3D model.
cases.body_notes: JetBrains used identical anatomy meshes and high reasoning effort. It described Sol’s opening as more dramatic and Astra’s depth and cutaways as easier to study.

cases.prompt: build a website for a hotel that doesn't exist
cases.title: A website for a fictional hotel
cases.takeaway: Compare one-shot layouts, elapsed time and cost on the same hotel brief.
cases.body_notes: The author ran both models at xhigh and reported 5m 52s and $4.71 for Sol Ultrafast, and 1h 53m and $41.11 for Opus 5.5.

cases.title: Design Creativity Bench for UI
cases.takeaway: Compare the benchmark’s creative design scores alongside reported cost.
cases.body_notes: Kombai published a creativity score of 70.0 for Sol and 70.4 for Astra and reported a lower cost per design for Sol.

cases.title: Browser Use task completion and step counts
cases.takeaway: Compare completion, time and steps on the same browser suite.
cases.body_notes: Browser Use reported 82% for Sol 6.2 and 81% for Sol 6.1. Its launch-day comparison also reports 12 versus 22 minutes and 36% fewer steps for 6.2.

cases.title: A butterfly gallery with Blender models
cases.takeaway: Combine a rotatable specimen with views for close inspection and field notes.
cases.body_notes: The creator attributed the site to Sol and Blender. The walkthrough shows a selection of animated butterflies, a magnifier for wing details, and panels for habitat, taxonomy and life stages.

cases.title: Perplexity’s WANDR agent benchmark
cases.takeaway: Compare task score and cost per task together.
cases.body_notes: Perplexity reported a WANDR score of 0.746 at about $2.65 per task for Sol, a 0.065 score increase over GPT-6.1 Sol on its benchmark.

cases.title: Finding GeoGuessr locations with browser controls
cases.takeaway: Keep starting locations, the time limit and the distance threshold fixed across models.
cases.body_notes: The tester gave each model the same 100 starts and five minutes per location to place a pin within 1 km. Sol and Astra both met the threshold 77 times. The tester reported Sol was the faster of the two.

cases.title: Navigating from 50 Wikipedia starting pages
cases.takeaway: Keep the destination and start pages fixed when timing navigation.
cases.body_notes: All five models reached Jacob Misiorowski’s page from every assigned start. The tester reports 39 seconds for Sol, the fastest result in that comparison.

cases.title: A Kanban plugin for agent sessions
cases.takeaway: Check how tasks, sessions and review queues connect in the interface.
cases.body_notes: The Super Kanban developer reports using Sol for two days of refactoring. The v0.8.0 release groups tasks across workspaces and connects a task to multiple sessions.

cases.title: A 360-degree Bugatti Chiron configurator
cases.takeaway: Compare paint finishes as the camera moves around the car.
cases.body_notes: The recording shows blue, silver and black finishes under studio lighting as the camera changes angle.

cases.title: Gravity balls in a rotating heptagon
cases.takeaway: Inspect how balls respond as their container rotates.
cases.body_notes: The browser recording shows a group of colored balls falling and collecting along the edges of a rotating seven-sided container.

请使用 Three.js 创作一个主题为《时间的尽头》的 3D 交互式网页。

cases.body_notes: The screen recording shows Island Atlas and Kame House, a day and night switch, and a conversation panel on the left.

cases.takeaway: Compare what two outputs do with the same reference before attributing the difference.
cases.body_notes: The clip includes an interface and 3D output. The author explicitly says the difference does not establish the backend model.

cases.takeaway: Compare intermediate frames with the reference shown next to the canvas.
cases.body_notes: The creator attributes the portrait to Sol. The recording shows the canvas progress from blank to a detailed likeness of Sam Altman.
